subtopics.name: Reasons for & Implications of Different Population Structures

parts.problem_md:
For a country, you have studied with a high young or old dependent population, describe the problems caused by this population structure. Circle your choice of young or old dependent population.

Name of country ..............................................

      Young dependent       Old dependent
parts.solution_md:
Levels marking | **Level 1 (1–3 marks)** | **Level 2 (4–6 marks)** | **Level 3 (7 marks)** | |---|---|---| | Statements including limited detail which describe the problems faced by a country with a large dependent population.
e.g. lack of workforce | Uses named example.

More developed statements which describe the problems faced by a country with a large dependent population, **not the reasons for them or the solutions.**

(**Note:** Max 5 if no named or inappropriate example) | Uses named example.
Comprehensive and accurate statements including some place specific reference. | Content Guide: Answers are likely to refer to old dependents but could also refer to young dependents. High dependency rate Stress on working population Increased taxation Lack of workforce Need to provide pensions Lack of innovation Difficulty recruiting armed forces Pressure on healthcare Under use of facilities for young people/closure of schools etc Positive effects Place specific reference is likely to consist of: Named parts/settlements of the chosen country, Population data, etc. on Place specific reference is likely to consist of: Named parts of the chosen country, Population data etc. Note: Can refer to young and/or old and don’t need to specify which. Place specific examples include: - *Locational details - where situated Japan* - *Specific details -* - *Japan's population in 2010 reached 128 million people and then decreased to 125 million by 2020* - *Its population change rate is -0.3%* - *Life expectancy has increased from an average of 77 years to 84.36 years* - *Examples of paragraphs which could be included in an answer to achieve Level 3:* - *The dependancy ratio in Japan has increased to 76 and is predicted to increase to 96% by 2050 this has led to an increase in taxes because an ageing population puts increasing pressure on health and social care, as well as increasing pension payments. There is predicted to be a shortage of 380,000 workers for elderly care by 2025. This reduces the amount of disposable income that the working age population have.* - *Schools and childcare facilities may close. The birth rate is 7.1 per 1000 and fertility rate 1.36 which is well below the 2.1 replacement rate. As a result fewer children are being born and needing these services and an average of 450 schools are closing each year. Resulting in the lists of jobs.*

parts.problem_md: For a named country you have studied, describe and explain the causes of an ageing population.
parts.solution_md:
| **Indicative Content** | **General Guidance** | |---|---| | Causes might include:

- Low birth rate
- Later / fewer marriages
- Good access to family planning/contraception
- Good education about family planning/contraception
- Smaller families
- Longer life expectancies
- Better healthcare
- Provision of pensions
- Better diets
- Education about diet/exercise | - The command word ‘describe’ requires you to state the key causes of having an ageing population
- The command word ‘explain’ requires you to say how and why these factors cause an ageing population
- This is a levelled response answer. It is important to remember that each point does not equate to a mark. The examiner will read your whole answer and make a decision about which level your answer fits into
- If you do not name a country, or the country you choose is not appropriate, a maximum of 5 marks will be awarded | | **Model Answer** | **Commentary** | |---|---| | Named country: Japan

A third of Japan’s population is over 60 years old, and 12% are over 75 years. This is due to a combination of low birth rates and a high life expectancy.

Japan has one of the highest life expectancies in the world at 84 years. This is because of a high-quality healthcare system that is accessible to everyone. People get regular health checks which help to detect diseases early and improve chances of recovery. The traditional Japanese diet is also very healthy, contributing to lower rates of obesity and heart disease. Finally, Japanese culture promotes the importance of an active lifestyle which leads to better health and fitness.

Japan also has a very low fertility rate of just 1.36 births per woman. This is well below the fertility replacement rate of 2.1. One reason for the low birth rate is the high cost of living. Many people struggle to afford to buy or rent their own homes and 70% of unmarried people live with their parents. High childcare costs make it very expensive to have children and job security has fallen in recent years. There is also a declining marriage rate and an increase in the average age at which people get married to 29.5 years for women and 31 years for men. This is partly due to the increasing number of women in the workforce. Japan’s work culture traditionally involves long working hours which can cause people to delay starting a family or to choose to have fewer or no children. | **Marks 7/7**

- This is one possible way to answer this question – your answer does not have to be exactly the same
- You need to refer to a named country in your answer
- Using phrases such ‘this is because’ and ‘this is partly due to’’ will help you extend your explanation
- You also need to include place specific detail such as statistics or specific details of causes in order to gain 7 marks
- This answer outlines several causes of an ageing population and develops them by quoting supporting facts and evidence |

parts.problem_md: For a named country you have studied, describe and explain the impacts of having a large percentage of dependent population.
parts.solution_md:
| **Indicative Content** | **General Guidance** | |---|---| | Impacts might include:

**Youthful population**

- A high dependency ratio
- Increased pressure on / cost of healthcare provision
- Increased pressure on schools/nurseries for young
- High unemployment rates
- Housing shortages
- Growth of informal settlements
- Food shortages
- Pressures on clean water supplies
- Increased rural-urban migration
- Increased emigration

**Ageing population**

- A high dependency ratio
- Increased pressure on / cost of healthcare provision
- Increased pressure on care homes/services for elderly
- Increased cost of pensions
- Shortages of workers
- Increased taxes
- Reduced tax income/revenue | - The command word ‘describe’ requires you to state the key impacts of having a large percentage of dependent population
- The command word ‘explain’ requires you to say how and why these impacts affect the country
- This is a levelled response answer. It is important to remember that each point does not equate to a mark. The examiner will read your whole answer and make a decision about which level your answer fits into
- If you do not name a country, or the country you choose is not appropriate, you will only gain a maximum of 5 marks | | **Model Answer** | **Commentary** | |---|---| | Named country: Niger

Niger’s population grew from 3.3 million in 1960 to nearly 25 million in 2021. Niger now has a high dependency ratio with almost 50% of the population aged below 15 years.

This has led to a number of problems such as increased pressure on farmland and food supplies. Food shortages are not uncommon, with an estimated 2.5 million people suffering from food insecurity. It is also very difficult to provide schooling for such a large youthful population and only 4 out of 10 girls in Niger finish primary school. This contributes to the continued high birth rates due to younger marriages and lack of education about contraception. The fertility rate in Niger is an average of seven children per woman – one of the highest fertility rates in the world.

Another challenge is providing enough job opportunities and housing for people. This has led to high rates of rural-urban migration as people seek jobs in the capital city Niamey. However, when they arrive in the city, people are faced with housing shortages and end up living in informal settlements on the edge of the city. High population densities lead to problems of overcrowding, poor hygiene and shortages of clean water. A lack of infrastructure means that there is inadequate sanitation and healthcare which can lead to the rapid spread of disease. These issues contribute to one of the highest infant mortality rates in the world, leading to people having more children to ensure that some survive into adulthood. This perpetuates the problem of a high dependency ratio. | **Marks 7/7**

- This is one possible way to answer this question – your answer does not have to be exactly the same
- You need to refer to a named country in your answer
- Using phrases such ‘this leads to’ and ‘this contributes to’ will help you extend your explanation
- You also need to include place specific detail such as named places within the country, statistics or specific details of impacts in order to gain 7 marks
- This answer outlines several problems and develops them by giving named examples of places and by quoting supporting evidence |

Study Figs. 1.1 and 1.2, which show the population structure for a rural and urban area in Tanzania (an LEDC in Africa).

What evidence in Figs. 1.1 and 1.2 suggests that:

....................................................

parts.solution_md:
**Birth rate is high in rural Ifakara:**
The base of the pyramid is wide **[1]**
More/there are large numbers of young dependents/lots of babies/children/0–4 year olds **[1]**

- *No marks will be received for information on age groups 5+*

**Life expectancy is low in rural Ifakara:**
Narrow top/apex/there are few old people/small percentage living above 65 years or reference to a single age band/no people live above 85 years **[1]**

parts.problem_md:
Study Fig. 1.1, which shows information about the population structure of Thailand (an LEDC in Southeast Asia) in 1980 and 2015.

How many of the population of Thailand in 1980 were female and aged 0 to 4?

.............................................million
parts.solution_md:
3 (millions) **[1]**

- *This question specifies female in 1980*
- *It is essential to use the correct population pyramid and look at the correct side of the graph *

parts.problem_md: Describe how the total population of Thailand aged 0 to 4 changed between 1980 and 2015. You should use statistics in your answer.
parts.solution_md:
Decreased/higher in 1980/lower in 2015/(almost) halved **[1]**

From 6.1/6.2 million to 3.4-3.6 (million)/by 2.5-2.8 million **[1]**

- *It is important in this case to give the total decrease rather than separating into males and females*
- *Take time to measure the graphs accurately, there is some leeway given with figures but not much *

parts.problem_md: Describe how the **shape** of Thailand’s population pyramid changed between 1980 and 2015.
parts.solution_md:
Ideas such as;
It became less triangular/pyramid shaped in 1980 but rounded in 2015/concave in 1980 convex in 2015 **[1]**
Base/young dependents became narrower/thinner **[1]**
Top/old dependents became wider/thicker **[1]**
Centre/economically active became wider **[1]**

- *The question refers to the shape of the population pyramid so you need to consider whether it is pyramid shaped or more column shaped. Is it convex or concave?*
- *Narrower and wider are the correct terms to use rather than bigger/smaller*
- *Marks will not be awarded for answers which write about 'young dependents decreasing' or 'old dependents increasing' you need to specifically mention how this affects the shape*

parts.problem_md:
Study Fig 1.2, which shows population pyramids of the structure of Mexico’s population in 1980 and 2010.

![q1-1b-0460-w19-qp-13](assets/006-q1-1b-0460-w19-qp-13.png)

Describe the changes in Mexico’s population structure between 1980 and 2010.
parts.solution_md:
Ideas such as:
More economically active/working/15–64 **[1]**
More young (dependents)/0–14/5–14/numbers in age bands up to 19 become more even **[1]**

- *When answering questions on population pyramids, divide the pyramid into three groups. For this question it has been done on the paper*

  - *Young dependents (Below age 15)*
  - *Working age/economically active (15-64)*
  - *Old dependents (65+)*
- *This question refers to the structure not the shape or specific age groups so it is important to write about the changes in the three broad groups*
- *The answer need to compare the two population pyramids stating 'more' or 'fewer' in your answer*

parts.problem_md:
Study Fig. 1.3, which is a population pyramid for the United Arab Emirates (UAE), an MEDC.

![q1b-0460-s20-qp-12](assets/005-q1b-0460-s20-qp-12.png)

Identify three characteristics of the population pyramid for the UAE which suggest that it attracts many migrants.
parts.solution_md:
Ideas such as:
Imbalanced sex distribution/more males/less females **[1]**
Few old dependents **[1]**
Mostly economically active are ages 20–50 **[1]**
Few young dependents/children ages0–19 **[1]**

- *Migrant populations are often dominated by males age 20-45 *
- *This means that the birth rate and % of young dependents is low as there is an imbalance between males and females in the population*
